title: (PDF) Bioavailability and Kinetics of Sulforaphane in Humans after Consumption of Cooked versus Raw Broccoli
abstract: # Bioavailability and Kinetics of Sulforaphane in Humans after Consumption of Cooked versus Raw Broccoli. The aim of this study was to determine the bioavailability and kinetics of the supposed anticarcinogen sulforaphane, the hydrolysis product of glucoraphanin, from raw and cooked broccoli. Higher amounts of sulforaphane were found in the blood and urine when broccoli was eaten raw (bioavailability of 37%) versus cooked (3.4%, p ) 0.002). This study gives complete kinetic data and shows that consumption of raw broccoli results in faster absorption, higher bioavailability, and higher peak plasma amounts of sulforaphane, compared to cooked broccoli. 1. Consumption of raw broccoli yields 37% bioavailability of sulforaphane, compared to 3.4% from cooked broccoli (p=0.002). What are the key differences in sulforaphane bioavailability from raw versus cooked broccoli? The study finds that sulforaphane bioavailability from raw broccoli is 37%, significantly higher than 3.4% from cooked broccoli (p = 0.002).
